plan_fields.label: Why are you a fit for this role?
plan_fields.reason: Essay generated from the operator's about-me context

fields.expected:
The part of the posting that fits me best is owning a focused research project on a stack that has to actually work in production. At Summer Atlantic Capital I built the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, and temporal sequence modeling over event streams using RNN and Transformer-style approaches, plus a learning-to-rank layer for alert prioritization. That work taught me that model metrics are only half the problem: an anomaly system that fires too often creates a second problem instead of solving the first, so failure modes and operational usefulness matter as much as the score.

I also care a lot about evaluation. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework for LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard, using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes rather than a single aggregate number. Generating an output is cheap; deciding whether to trust it is the hard part, and that applies directly to speech-to-text, codecs, and TTS.

I have not worked on speech models before, but I learn by building, and I want to work on the same problems the research team is on.
